title: My New Life Began With the clerk assigned to the Demon King and the Demon King Sent Me an Invoice
synopsis: A supposedly legendary hero discovers that the kingdom's greatest threat is an administrative error with a sword. The story unfolds in The Archipelago of Suspiciously Convenient Prophecies, where prophecies become stronger when people misunderstand them. The central problem is a Demon King whose greatest weapon is administrative patience. Milo Kestrel wants to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot, but every reasonable solution creates a new unreasonable obligation.
premise: A supposedly legendary hero discovers that the kingdom's greatest threat is an administrative error with a sword.
authorNotes: Please remember that the bureaucracy is fictional. The paperwork is not.

world.rule: Prophecies become stronger when people misunderstand them.
world.oddity: Every prophecy has at least one typo.
world.magic: Contract magic turns promises, receipts, and signatures into real spells.
world.threat: a Demon King whose greatest weapon is administrative patience

chapters.title: Nobody Prepared Me For the World's Least Useful Sword — Milo Kestrel POV
chapters.arcTitle: The Problem With The Original Plan
paragraphs: CHAPTER 1 — Milo Kestrel POV
The Problem With The Original Plan had already produced two meetings, one argument, and a document nobody could legally throw away.
Milo Kestrel arrived at the old dungeon intending to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot. The plan lasted until the first unexpected detail appeared.
Two factions interpret the same sentence in completely different ways.
Milo Kestrel recorded the incident as objectively as circumstances permitted.
The important object was a rubber stamp. It was not magical in the usual sense, which made it considerably more suspicious.
Milo Kestrel checked the obvious explanation first. It was wrong. They checked the ridiculous explanation next. It was unfortunately closer.
The world of The Archipelago of Suspiciously Convenient Prophecies followed one inconvenient rule: Prophecies become stronger when people misunderstand them.
The conversation became quieter when everyone realized that the newest clue had a date older than the kingdom itself.
The official version would later contain considerably fewer mistakes than the actual version.
A second person arrived carrying information about the contradictory prophecy. Their explanation contradicted the first explanation in exactly the way a useful clue should.
Nobody agreed on what to do with the rubber stamp. One person wanted to destroy it. Another wanted to file it. Milo Kestrel wanted to know why it had appeared here.
That question led to a small discovery: Milo Kestrel has a private connection to the prophecy.
The mystery remained open, although Milo Kestrel now had one useful fact: someone was treating the contradictory prophecy as if it were a normal administrative matter.
Before leaving, Milo Kestrel made a decision that would matter later: they would not trust the next official document until they had read the footnotes.
For the first time that day, everyone agreed on something. This was probably going to get worse.
